concepts.title: 01 — Type
concepts.prompt:
Create a high-fidelity, finished WEB DESIGN RENDER for Bremray Electrical, a residential electrician in Ann Arbor, Michigan. It is a visual concept, not a code screenshot of the existing site. Render a full desktop homepage, from navigation through a useful lower-page section and footer, flat front-on with no device frame, no browser chrome, no angled perspective. Use a tall canvas about 1440 wide by 2000 high. The UI should feel considered, beautiful and buildable. Keep all text sharp and legible. Realistic website spacing and type scale, not a poster pretending to be a website.
Use these exact texts with correct spelling:
Brand: "Bremray Electrical"
Visible header phone immediately beside the brand: "(734) 216-9437"
Navigation: "Services" "About" "Contact"
Main prominent H1: "Licensed electrician in Ann Arbor."
Lead-entry question: "What do you need done?"
Three intent choices: "Install something new" "Replace or upgrade" "Something isn’t working"
Secondary choice: "I’d rather type"
Useful lower content headings: "What will it cost?" and "Electrical work for your home."
Useful service names: "EV chargers" "Generators" "Panel upgrades" "Lighting & repairs"
Cost text: "Tell us a little about the job. We’ll help work out what’s involved and get back to you about the price."
Location/hours: "Ann Arbor & Washtenaw County" and "Monday–Friday · 8am–5pm"
Footer: "Bremray Electrical" and "(734) 216-9437".
The lead interaction belongs immediately in the first screen, and the local electrician heading must be conspicuous. The customer comes to get help quickly. Do not make this a generic marketing hero with a giant photograph and a CTA. Use short, normal language. No invented prices, ratings, customer quotes, certifications, reviews, guarantees or project counts. No SPAN promotion, commercial/industrial promotion, free quote slogans, instant estimate promise, cartoon mascot, gradient, glassmorphism, gold, dark green, navy, or beige. Do not imitate the previous contractor layout. Treat the typographic brand treatment as a concept rather than inventing a pictorial logo.
ART DIRECTION 1: PURE WHITE + BLACK, TYPOGRAPHY DOES THE WORK. Sophisticated Swiss graphic design meets a practical local business. Strictly white paper, near-black ink, a little neutral gray. Use very large tightly spaced bold condensed grotesk headline typography reminiscent of Archivo Black or a fine newspaper sans; normal readable grotesk body. A small but strong black Bremray wordmark and phone share a compact top strip; narrow navigation at far right. CENTER the enormous headline across two deliberate lines, with lots of white surrounding it, not a banner background. Under the headline place the question and three strong typographic intent controls as three open, unboxed columns on the same horizontal baseline, with large meaningful words, subtle secondary labels, and small directional arrows. An active "Install something new" choice is black-filled only around its compact text control, not a giant card. Below it reveal an elegantly aligned compact second-row question "What do you want us to install?" with outlined pill-like text choices "Lights" "An EV charger" "A ceiling fan" "Something else". The entire opening should look like a confident typesetter built a useful tool, not an FAQ or accordion and not a dashboard. No photographs in this direction. Lower-page content becomes an arresting asymmetrical editorial composition: huge black "What will it cost?" on the left and a narrow plain answer column on the right, then an unboxed service index with varied type weights and horizontal rules. Finish with an oversized black typographic footer. Generous but disciplined whitespace, precise optical alignment, fewer things on screen, strong readable hierarchy.

ART DIRECTION 2: LOCAL EDITORIAL, ELEGANT BLACK SERIF ON WHITE WITH A TINY BRICK RED ACCENT. This composition must be completely different from a centered headline plus three columns. Use expressive contemporary editorial serif headings similar to Newsreader Display, italic only for a small supporting phrase, paired with quiet humanist sans body text. Small white masthead, thin black rules, brick-red tiny dots/section numbers only. Opening is a composed newspaper-like asymmetric grid: LEFT TWO THIRDS has the large left-aligned H1 wrapping naturally over three lines, with a narrow side caption for location and hours; RIGHT THIRD is a clean white "Start here" request column with the question and three plain typographic choices stacked with fine separators and a restrained black round arrow on each, not bordered cards. Do not make the request index look like an FAQ: use action phrasing and large numbered navigation, no plus icons. Below the top headline area, an editorial black-and-white, slightly grainy, casually photographed close-up of neatly organized residential electrical wiring occupies a horizontal crop on the left, with a tiny "Illustrative image" caption; it is not a fake customer job claim and contains no person or unsafe activity. Below, use magazine-style narrow and wide columns, prominent section headings, an understated cost explanation, and a thoughtful service directory rather than card tiles. Headings are much more visible than supporting text. There is no hero image behind text, no cream background, no generic luxury aesthetic. The impression is an intelligent, established local trade business: human, calm and precise. The footer is small and editorial, not a giant colored band.

ART DIRECTION 3: COBALT + WHITE, A USEFUL SERVICE DESK. Radically different asymmetric layout and navigation from the other two. Bright true cobalt blue #254BFF, pure white, cool light gray, black text; no navy. Use IBM Plex Sans style humanist/workmanlike typography with only tiny monospaced labels for step numbers. A slim vertical cobalt identity rail runs along the LEFT quarter of the opening screen and holds Bremray Electrical, clearly visible phone beside/below it, simple small navigation, and location/hours. On the RIGHT three quarters, a white open working area begins with the prominent black H1 and then the active request form. Form state is inviting and clearly usable, not a corporate dashboard: a small progress line "1 / Tell us what you need" and large question. Arrange intent controls as an asymmetric typographic tile pattern: one wide cobalt primary tile for "Install something new", then two compact white controls below for "Replace or upgrade" and "Something isn’t working", bordered only by black hairlines, with big simple arrow symbols; the grid is integrated into the page rather than floating cards. Beneath the selected installation option show a compact row of practical next choices "Lights" "EV charger" "Generator" "Something else". Include "I’d rather type" as a quiet text link. No photo and no conventional hero at all. Below the opening, let the white page span the entire width into a numbered service directory with four broad rows and clear information, not marketing cards. Put "What will it cost?" in a narrow cobalt text column beside a plain black answer on white. The footer repeats the cobalt left-rail motif. Bold color geometry, functional typographic hierarchy, energetic yet calm, ample whitespace, square edges. No tiny ghost labels, no pointless admin charts or fabricated metrics.
